How is this offset handled for a push32 when the chunk size is less than 32 bytes <@!461762841641484302> can I ask which segment that is? I'm confused because I'm getting different results (segments-9090000, binary tree, 32-byte hashes). Also the number of hashes are increasing with the chunk size in the results you shared, but intuitively they should decrease (lower tree depth) ``` 1-byte chunks: running total: blocks=1000 overhead=283.3% exec=57093.0K merklization=218830.7K = 57093.0 K chunks + 161737.7 K hashes estimated median:23.0 16-byte chunks: running total: blocks=1000 overhead=129.3% exec=57093.0K merklization=130905.6K = 66553.9 K chunks + 64351.8 K hashes estimated median:23.0 32-byte chunks: running total: blocks=1000 overhead=116.6% exec=57093.0K merklization=123666.9K = 73792.6 K chunks + 49874.2 K hashes estimated median:23.0 64-byte chunks: running total: blocks=1000 overhead=116.6% exec=57093.0K merklization=123666.9K = 86801.6 K chunks + 36865.2 K hashes estimated median:23.0 ``` You might notice something curious in my results: proof size for 32-byte chunks and 64-byte is exactly the same. I thought it's coincidence but I ran it for multiple segments and it was always like that. No idea why, I'll have to dig deeper sidenote: it's cool to be able to just try all combinations of arity, chunkSize, etc. so easily, thanks for the tool! > How is this offset handled for a push32 when the chunk size is less than 32 bytes I've been setting `offset = chunkSize` for the data-only chunks, but in lower chunk sizes these data chunks will be more prevalent and we might be better off with a different trick (like storing offset only for non-data chunks in metadata) <@!636680106630316033> this is a calculation for hashes in a simple merkle tree, with no consideration for that kind of metadata, since that should be much smaller and dependent on the final format of the data itself. <@!259648573401071617> try importing the module and just using the merklize() function with any random list of chunks, it's really illuminating! (deleted a bunch of messages for clarity) First of all, the segments file 9090000 is one of only 2 in the range 9M-10M with a median >20. The median for that whole range is <15, so I *guess* that there can be some statistical weirdness. To avoid this kind of problem I've uploaded to the releases section of the tool an index file with the per-block, per-file and global stats for the range. Having said that, I'm not sure how much that matters. Still looking into it. I don't understand what has changed in the code to justify the difference, but now both files 9000000 and 9090000 seem to have a minimum overhead of ~110% around chunk size 48 (better than 44 or 52). Chunks smaller than 32 do increasingly terrible. I don't get it! 😩 I'll push my changes and try taking a fresher look in the morning. I have deleted the overheads table in the Ethresear.ch article and added a couple of warnings. > <@!636680106630316033> this is a calculation for hashes in a simple merkle tree, with no consideration for that kind of metadata, since that should be much smaller and dependent on the final format of the data itself. <@!461762841641484302> For small chunk sizes, the metadata would have a big impact. For example, if the chunk size was 4 bytes, then an extra byte to indicate the start of the first opcode adds 25% overhead.

excerpts.content:
> How is this offset handled for a push32 when the chunk size is less than 32 bytes
I've been setting `offset = chunkSize` for the data-only chunks, but in lower chunk sizes these data chunks will be more prevalent and we might be better off with a different trick (like storing offset only for non-data chunks in metadata)
